title: Jabal Ḏabūb inscription (South Arabian graffito, Late Sabaic)
language_note: Late Sabaic (minuscule variant), Old South Arabian script. First published 2018 (Al-Hajj & Faq'as); reading revised by Ahmad Al-Jallad in 2022.
findspot: Mount Thaboob (Jabal Ḏabūb), Dhale region, Yemen
original_text_excerpt: bs¹mlh | rḥmn | rḥmn | rb | s¹mwt / r{z}{q}n | mfḍlk | wʾṯrn | mḫh | s²kmt ʾymn
original_text_note: Transliteration of the Sabaic minuscule text per Al-Jallad's 2022 revised reading (supersedes the 2018 editio princeps).
reference_translation: In the name of Allah, the Rahman — have mercy upon us, O lord of the heavens; satisfy us by means of your favor; and grant us the essence of it at the end/gift of our days.
translation_source: Ahmad Al-Jallad, 'A pre-Islamic basmala: reflections on its first epigraphic attestation and its original significance', Jerusalem Studies in Arabic and Islam 52 (2022): 1–28.
notes: Chronologically later than most of the Persia/East Asia seed sources (6th c.) and not directly about Rome, but it is the concrete, openly-documented Sabaic candidate for the region and demonstrates the pre-Islamic South Arabian religious vocabulary (Rahmanan) relevant to Red Sea contact narratives. Consider supplementing with a denser, more directly Rome-linked Sabaic/Himyarite inscription (e.g. a Ma'rib dam or Sabaean-Himyarite royal inscription) in a later pass if the region needs a stronger Roman-contact anchor.

findspot_places.name: Jabal Ḏabūb
findspot_places.note: **Both GeoNames candidates were examined and REFUSED**, on feature type and on coordinate. 7365997 'Ad Dabūb' 15.944/43.437 and 12118329 'Ad Dabūb' 14.519/43.601 are both P.PPL — *populated places*, where the record names a mountain (Arabic *jabal*), and GeoNames classes mountains T.MT. Both also sit far outside the region the record gives: 286 km and 152 km respectively from Ad Dali', in the Dhale region of southern Yemen. A settlement called Ad Dabūb is not Mount Ḏabūb, and neither is in the right place. Nothing resolves in either gazetteer; what is known is the region, Dhale, and no more.
